summary: John Kieschnick is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and history and archaeology. He held a post at the University of Bristol (~2005–2011) and became Robert H. N. Ho Family Foundation Professor of Buddhist Studies at Stanford University (~2011).

John Lane Bell is a philosopher who studied at Lick-Wilmerding High School and the University of Oxford (~1963–1968). He held positions at the London School of Economics (~1968–1989), the University of Western Ontario (~1989), and the National University of Singapore.

John Lockwood Kipling, educated at Woodhouse Grove School, worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He taught at Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art (~1865–1875), served as Principal of the National College of Arts (1875–1893), and curated Lahore Museum (1875–1893).

John M. Koller is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena and Charles Alexander Moore. He served as a professor of philosophy at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (attested 1988, 1999).

John M. Rosenfield was an art historian and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Harvard under Benjamin Rowland. He taught at Iowa and UCLA before serving as professor (1965–1991) and art museum director (~1982–1991) at Harvard.

John Marshall was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Cambridge and the British School at Athens under Arthur Evans. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1902–1931) and belonged to the British Academy.

John Muir was an Indologist who studied at Glasgow, East India Company College, and Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853), was principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1844), and held a post at the University of Edinburgh.
John Myrdhin Reynolds is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He pursued traditional studies under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (~1971–1987) and Namkhai Norbu (~1979–2018).

John Nemec is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Rochester, UCSB, Oxford, and Penn (PhD 2005), where he studied under Alexis Sanderson and Ludo Rocher. He is Associate Professor of Indian Religions at the University of Virginia (attested 2020).

John Newman is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (-1987) under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, also studying under Geshe Wangdrak. He served as Assistant Professor at New College of Florida (attested 1996–2000).

John Okell was a linguist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford (~1953–1957) and under Hla Pe, Anna J. Allott, and Richard Keith Sprigg. He served as a research associate at SOAS University of London (1959–1999).

John P. Keenan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He was a research fellow at Nanzan University (1983–1986) and professor at Middlebury College (attested 1989, 2006).

John Peile was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Christ's College, Cambridge, and under Theodor Benfey (~1869). He served as Reader of Comparative Philology at Cambridge (1884–1891), Fellow at Christ's College (~1860–1910), and President of Newnham College (~1890–1909).
John Pickford was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He later served as a professor at the University of Madras.

John Powers is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He has held posts at the Australian National University (1995), Deakin University (2016–2022), and the University of Melbourne (2022).

John R. B. Campbell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb. He also studied under Tenzin Gyatso, Denma Lochö Rinpoche, and Gyumed Khensur Lobsang Ngawang.

John R. McRae was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD from Yale under Stanley Weinstein and studied under Seizan Yanagida. He taught at Cornell (~1987–1995), Indiana University (~1996–2005), and Komazawa and Soka universities.

John Raines was a religious studies scholar who studied at Carleton College (~1951–1955) and Union Theological Seminary (~1956–1959). He held an academic post at Temple University from approximately 1970 to 2011.
John Riley Perks is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied traditionally under Dilgo Khyentse and the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

John Ross Carter was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed doctoral work at Harvard under Wilfred Cantwell Smith, after studying at King's College London and SOAS. He served as a professor at Colgate University (~1972–2006).
